title: Programming paradigms: applied comparison
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: How does OOP differ from a procedural program?
questions.answer: OOP groups state and behaviour into objects; procedural code is organised around procedures/functions.
options: OOP groups state and behaviour into objects; procedural code is not organised around procedures/functions.
OOP groups state and behaviour into objects; procedural code is organised around procedures/functions.
OOP groups state OR behaviour into objects; procedural code is organised around procedures/functions.
questions.feedback: Model answer: OOP groups state and behaviour into objects; procedural code is organised around procedures/functions.

questions.prompt: What does a local variable mean?
questions.answer: A variable accessible only within its declaration's scope.
options: A variable accessible only within its declaration's scope.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
This result cannot be obtained using the stated method.
questions.feedback: Model answer: A variable accessible only within its declaration's scope.

questions.prompt: If a field is private-set, how can callers change it safely?
questions.answer: Through public methods/property logic defined by the class.
options: There is not enough information to determine the result.
This result cannot be obtained using the stated method.
Through public methods/property logic defined by the class.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Through public methods/property logic defined by the class.

questions.prompt: Why does `Deposit(balance,5);` not update the caller's int balance if only a return value is produced?
questions.answer: The return is discarded and a value-type parameter is a copy; the caller must assign the returned result.
options: The print is discarded and a value-type parameter is a copy; the caller must assign the returned result.
The return is discarded and a value-type parameter is a copy; the caller must assign the returned result.
The return is discarded OR a value-type parameter is a copy; the caller must assign the returned result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: The return is discarded and a value-type parameter is a copy; the caller must assign the returned result.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: refactoring — Restructuring code while preserving expected behaviour.
encapsulation — Controlled access to internal state.
instance — Individual object created from a class.
return value — Output returned to the caller.
side effect — Observable change beyond a returned result.

blocks.title: Procedural state
blocks.text: The caller passes an integer balance and explicitly stores the returned value.

blocks.title: Object state
blocks.text: Account object A stores Balance internally and Deposit changes that object's state.

blocks.title: Separate instances
blocks.text: Account B stays at 20 when Account A changes to 15; the objects have independent state.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model response
blocks.text: Account b remains at 20 because its state is separate.
